item.title: Netanyahu Opponents in Parliament Move to Undo His Key Policies
item.description: Israel’s newly-elected lawmakers unveiled a series of bills targeting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on the day the new Knesset was sworn in, a sign his rivals are eager to undo his political legacy after their recent election victory.
item.dc:creator: Galit Altstein

item.title: Stocks Gain on AI Optimism Despite US Inflation Concerns
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Berlin, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Global stocks climbed as investor enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence trade outweighed concern that hotter-than-expected US inflation will prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates further.
CoreWeave eased fears about its debt-laden business during a high-stakes quarterly report, indicating that sales growth remains strong despite challenges facing the data center industry.
Plus, Anthropic’s bankers are weighing plans to increase the company’s valuation in its IPO to $1.5 trillion or more, the Financial Times reported.
Today's guest: Christian Bruch, Siemens Energy, CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spain’s Main Unions Hold Nationwide Strike Over Housing Costs
item.description: A national strike is expected to cause widespread disruption across Spain on Wednesday, as unions demand for more affordable housing.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gualtieri

item.title: Bangladesh Prosecutor Says Hasina Can’t Appeal Death Sentence
item.description: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has exhausted all legal options to challenge her death sentence and now faces execution, Aminul Islam, the country’s chief war-crimes prosecutor, said.
item.dc:creator: Arun Devnath

item.title: Russia Says Two Polish Spies Detained in Kaliningrad Region
item.description: Russia’s Federal Security Service detained two Polish citizens accused of spying in the Kaliningrad region, the Interfax news service reported Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Tony Halpin

item.title: US Envoy to China Says Relations Are ‘Bumpy’ After Nvidia Affair
item.description: The top US diplomat in China indicated that the furor over Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy was posing a test to bilateral relations — comments that come just as the leaders of the two nations prepare to meet.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Oil Edges Higher as US-Iran War Outlook in Focus
item.description: Oil gained after a two-day decline, as traders weigh the outlook for an end to the US-Iran war. US President Donald Trump said further strikes on Iran wouldn’t be necessary, but regional flareups have persisted and talks have shown little progress. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia’s Baltic Commodity Hub on Fire After Drone Attack
item.description: A drone attack sparked a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga, one of Russia’s biggest Baltic commodity-export hubs, raising the risk of disruptions to energy and grain shipments as Moscow and Kyiv prepare for a second day of US-mediated peace talks.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Poland’s Nawrocki Rally Appearance Risks Fueling Tension
item.description: Poland’s president is set to attend a rally organized by far-right groups on Independence Day, risking an increase in political tensions as the country navigates the aftermath of its deadliest shooting in decades.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Ojewska

item.title: Thailand to Raise Arsenic-Tainted Cross-Border Rivers in Talks With Myanmar
item.description: Thailand will seek urgent action from Myanmar over suspected mining pollution in cross-border rivers after arsenic levels surged to as much as 30 times the Thai standard, threatening drinking water and farmland in the country’s north.
item.dc:creator: Erich Parpart

item.title: Bessent Hails US-China Engagement, Sees More Exchanges on AI
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent hailed an improvement in US-China engagement ahead of President Donald Trump’s visit to the Asian nation next week, and said he expects further dialogue on artificial intelligence models.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Gu and Yash Roy

item.title: US-led ‘Squad’ Defense Bloc Eyes Coordination Hub in Philippines
item.description: The US, Japan, Australia and the Philippines agreed to establish a coordination hub in the Philippines and synchronize efforts to strengthen the archipelago’s defenses amid growing Chinese pressure in the region.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: House Takes up Hegseth Impeachment Procedural Vote
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, New York Republican Congressman Nick LaLota reacts to Jim Jordan’s election as incoming House minority leader, while praising Steve Scalise’s record and political skills. Arizona Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, says what he describes as efforts to sidestep Congress on war powers provide “good grounds” for Pete Hegseth’s impeachment, while saying he would review the evidence before any Senate trial. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public. The Claude chatbot maker and its co-founders are looking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with shares marketed for $70 to $78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.
On today’s episode:
Anthony Hughes, Bloomberg News Equity Capital Market Reporter Matthew Luzzetti, Chief US Economist, Deutsche Bank Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Melissa Smith, President & CEO, Wex (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Gallego Sees ‘Good Grounds’ for Hegseth Impeachment
item.description: Arizona Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, says what he describes as efforts to sidestep Congress on war powers provide “good grounds” for Pete Hegseth’s impeachment, while saying he would review the evidence before any Senate trial. Sen. Gallego also calls for scrutiny of whether outside influence played a role in Nvidia’s push to loosen chip export controls on China, and says the crypto industry will have to talk to returning Sen. Sherrod Brown and “ask for some forgiveness” after spending heavily against him. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kennedy Family Seeks to Intervene in Fight to Block Trump Arch
item.description: Members of the Kennedy family are seeking to intervene in the legal fight to block construction of a triumphal arch in Washington championed by President Donald Trump, saying it would interfere with memorial gravesites of family members — including JFK’s eternal flame.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Rep. LaLota ‘Bullish’ on Bipartisan Lame-Duck Deals
item.description: New York Republican Congressman Nick LaLota reacts to Jim Jordan’s election as incoming House minority leader, while praising Steve Scalise’s record and political skills. Rep. LaLota says he’s confident Republicans can work with Democrats on affordability and other shared priorities, and says he’s “bullish” Congress can use the lame-duck session to make progress on government funding and other bipartisan legislation. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s $10 Billion Suit Against BBC Beats Dismissal Attempt
item.description: A federal judge ruled that President Donald Trump can proceed with his $10 billion lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corp. over a misleading edit of a speech he gave to supporters before they attacked the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: House Republicans Thwart Massie’s Effort to Impeach Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans blocked the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for US military actions in the Middle East and Latin America, effectively killing the effort until Democrats take over Congress in January.
item.dc:creator: Roxana Tiron and Erik Wasson

item.title: Burnham Rejects EU Financial Rules, Shows Brexit Reset Limit
item.description: Andy Burnham’s government won’t accept so-called dynamic alignment of the UK’s financial services rules with those of the European Union, a stance that raises questions about the premier’s wider ambitions for closer ties.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Alberto Nardelli
